articles.title: Roadworks Scheduled on Nowell Road and Pershore Road in Middleton on 26 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on The Esplanade will commence on 4 October 2026, resulting in temporary road closures.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that roadworks on The Esplanade will begin on 4 October 2026. The works are scheduled to take place overnight, although the exact start date will be confirmed and signed on site prior to commencement.

The roadworks will involve a temporary closure of The Esplanade, starting at the junction with St Mary's Gate and extending 20 metres eastward. During this period, there will be no alternative route available for vehicles.

A marshal will be present on site to facilitate safe access to nearby car parks. Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the closure may impact local traffic flow.

For further information, including a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Appoints Paul Roberts as Permanent Chair
articles.excerpt: Paul Roberts has been appointed as the permanent chair of Rochdale Boroughwide Housing, succeeding interim chair Larry Gold. This decision aims to strengthen leadership within the organisation.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has appointed Paul Roberts as its new permanent chair, effective immediately. He succeeds Larry Gold, who served as the interim chair during the transition period.

Roberts brings extensive experience from various leadership roles within the housing sector. His appointment is expected to enhance the strategic direction of the organisation.

The decision to appoint a permanent chair follows a review aimed at providing stability and continuity in leadership for Rochdale Boroughwide Housing.

As chair, Roberts will focus on addressing housing needs in the borough and improving services for residents. Further details on his plans are expected in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Restoration of Historic Packer Spout Steps Completed in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, over 400 years old, has been completed, linking Rochdale Town Hall to St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough.
articles.content_html:
The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a unique set of historic steps over 400 years old, has been completed in the heart of Rochdale town centre. These steps, which run through the Broadfield Park Slopes, connect the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, with parts dating back to Saxon times.

Dating from before 1660, the Packer Spout steps have a rich history, believed to have been used by mourning relatives who would ascend to St Chad’s Church to scatter rue and rosemary in the churchyard as offerings for their loved ones. The steps were situated in a notorious slum area during the Victorian period, known as ‘the gank’, characterised by tightly packed housing and high crime rates, where many mill workers lived.

The restoration project, carried out by Oldham contractor Maysand, required innovative engineering solutions due to the steepness of the site. A special pulley system with tracks and rollers was devised to transport the stone up the hill. The team painstakingly removed all 122 steps, many of which were broken and uneven, before reconstructing the area underneath and the steps themselves using traditional sandstone to match the existing stone.

The completion of this restoration not only preserves a significant piece of Rochdale's history but also enhances the connectivity between key historical sites in the town centre, potentially attracting more visitors and fostering a greater appreciation for the local heritage.

articles.title: Pakistan Refuses to Repatriate Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader
articles.excerpt: During a meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar stated that there is no mechanism for extraditing Shabir Ahmed, a key figure in the Rochdale grooming gang.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

16:46, 28 August 2026

During a meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar stated that there is no mechanism for extraditing Shabir Ahmed, a key figure in the Rochdale grooming gang.

Pakistan has declined the United Kingdom's request to extradite Shabir Ahmed, a ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang, during a meeting between UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar.

Ishaq Dar stated that there is 'no bilateral mechanism' in place to facilitate the return of Ahmed, who has been convicted of child sexual exploitation in the UK.

The refusal comes amid ongoing discussions about the UK government's efforts to address issues related to child exploitation and the management of offenders abroad.

This development may have implications for local authorities in Rochdale as they continue to deal with the aftermath of the grooming scandal.
